captions.detailed: A tower-mounted, two-branch rotary stand featuring a heavy, tiered black base and a central grey vertical tower. Two radial arms are mounted on separate collars along the tower: a lower blue arm and an upper orange arm. Each arm acts as a single rigid member terminating in a small black circular pad with a vertical silver pin. Both arms independently rotate about the vertical axis of the central tower via revolute joints.
captions.instruction: Create a 3D model of a tower-mounted two-branch rotary stand. It should feature a heavy, stepped circular base in black, supporting a central grey vertical cylindrical tower with a black cap. Mount two radial arms on separate collars along the tower—one blue on the lower section and one orange on the upper section—each ending in a black circular tip with a silver vertical pin. Model both arms as independent revolute joints revolving around the central tower.
captions.factory: Construct the base using stacked cylinders of decreasing diameters. Create the central tower as a tall cylinder with a thin, slightly wider cylinder on top as the cap. For each of the two arms, construct a collar using a cylinder with a central hole, extrude a rectangular horizontal arm from its side, and add a small circular pad with a vertical pin at the outer tip. Position the lower arm collar (blue) and the upper arm collar (orange) at different heights along the tower, defining revolute joints for each about the vertical Z-axis.
